card.name: Serimpi
card.tagline: Refined Javanese court dance for four female dancers
card.profile: The Srimpi (also Serimpi) is a ritualized classical Javanese court dance associated with the royal palaces of Yogyakarta and Surakarta (Wikipedia). Usually performed by four female dancers, it shares its aesthetics, technique and costume with the bedhaya and is called its 'sister,' though it is less sacred. Its four dancers are seen as representing the four universal elements (earth, water, fire, air) and the cardinal directions; the composition depicts a stylized kris-dagger battle between heroines. Developed during the Mataram Dynasty, srimpi was used to train palace princesses and, when court dances began to be taught outside the kraton in the 1910s, became the basis of Javanese classical female dance.
card.insight: Because it lacks the bedhaya's full aura of sacredness, srimpi was the court dance chosen to be taught publicly beyond palace walls, making it the foundation of broader Javanese classical female dance training (Asian Traditional Theatre & Dance, Theatre Academy Helsinki).
card.image_significance: The 'sister of Bedhaya' — four elements. A representative image shows gilded costume, angular hand poses and a temple or court setting — Central Java courts, Indonesia.
